hypothesis: H52: for selected strict JavaScript lexical function declarations, an explicit source-level binding-scope collision scan and conservative direct-write scan can close the H51 function+var ambiguity gap without treating unrelated inner bindings as the same target. This remains static advisory context, never runtime identity or general dataflow analysis.
policy: Function declarations in a function body share that function binding scope; strict block functions remain in their selected block scope.
var declarations hoist to nearest function/source scope; let/const use selected lexical block/function-body scope; catch bindings handled separately.
A second declaration of the same name in that binding scope causes ambiguity abstention even if checker symbol lists omit it.
Any written direct assignment/update to the selected checker binding, or any property/element write on that binding, causes conservative abstention regardless of control flow/order.
Do not claim assignment executes, property write changes a call target, or all indirect/dynamic writes are detected. No runtime guarantee after a clean scan.
No broad support for sloppy AnnexB/with/eval/destructuring/loop-scope inference; global dynamic-scope indicator causes whole-file advisory abstention. Unhandled forms remain limitations.
Owned controls are research observations, not permanent test scaffolding. No upstream/app source execution.
acceptance: Measure unchangedV1 then newV2 on exact owned cases; retain raw outputs and distinguish false abstention from unsafe reference retention. Reapply V2 to exposed frozen Fastify only after controls review; no claim of independent semantic/runtime accuracy.
